properties.description:
One shared helper bounds any tool reply to a caller-supplied `budget_chars`: prose is cut progressively (4000/2000/800/240/120/0 characters) while numbers, counts and ids are never touched, and every trimmed reply carries a `budget` block naming what went and how to get it back. Shortening a LIST is opt-in and forbidden by default, so a vocabulary or catalogue comes back complete-and-terse rather than complete-and-empty; an 80-character floor keeps names, ids and enum values intact at every rung. Document-shaped payloads (the design export, the instruction set, a published surface) are excluded and instead WITHHOLD WHOLE over budget, naming the narrower call that works. A CI gate seeds a real design from the committed export, calls every no-argument read tool, and fails on any reply that exceeds the budget without declaring a bound — and fails equally when NOTHING overflowed, because a detector with nothing to run on must not read as one that ran clean.

2026-10-12 (59553c771, chg:a-bounded-reply-shortens-every-list-by-its-cost-and-compare-designs-pages-one-2026-10-12): under Sampling::Allowed, list length now gives across EVERY object-reachable list by the characters each costs (a heap takes one tail entry at a time from the costliest list, floor one entry), the assembled reply is re-measured WITH its budget block each round, and the block carries lists_shortened [{path, shown, total}]. Before, one list chosen by element count was halved to one entry while the others stayed whole, and the block was not counted, so a multi-list reply (compare_designs on two unrelated designs) stayed far over budget. Two unit tests pin it (failed first: 63,662 chars against 2,000; 1,582 against 1,500). The Forbidden path and every earlier test are unchanged. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.name: Every oversized reply offers a bound, trims prose before length, and a CI gate fails when it had nothing to run on
